newsitem.title: USA: San Jose, Calif., warns of tax measure's impact.
newsitem.headline: San Jose, Calif., warns of tax measure's impact.

text.p: A controversial California tax measure approved by voters earlier this month will put pressure on the city of San Jose's revenues over the long-term, the city's mayor warned.
"Over the long run, Proposition 218 will prevent San Jose from securing revenues to pay for additional services as our population increases," San Jose Mayor Susan Hammer said.

Proposition 218, approved by voters on November 5, strengthens existing law to require local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It also allows property owners to approve assessments and strictly limits fees and charges.
In response to the measure, Hammer said the city should begin "a slow and careful review" of its land use policies.

"There is no reason to rush into any changes," Hammer said in her November budget message for fiscal year 1997-1998. "But over the long run, we have to find ways for residential growth to pay for the services new households require."

As part of her budget announcement, Hammer said San Jose should achieve a $2.2 million surplus in its operating budget next year. She said revenues from construction activity have increased significantly, generating more resources for the city's capital programs.
Proposition 218 has drawn fire from local government officials throughout California.
The Los Angeles City Council recently decided to sue over the measure.
Moody's Investors Service Inc has warned that the credit ratings of some local governments in the state could be undermined by the tax measure.
